title: Chicken Korma
subtitle: Mild, creamy chicken curry with almonds and coconut
excerpt: Chicken thighs braised in a mild, aromatic sauce of onion, yoghurt, ground almonds, coconut milk, and warm spices. Fragrant and gently rich rather than hot.

recipe.sourceNotes: Korma is a Mughal cooking technique in which meat is braised in a sauce of yoghurt and ground nuts until the fat separates and the sauce becomes rich and concentrated. The word derives from the Urdu 'qorma', meaning braise. The dish reached Britain through the Bangladeshi and Pakistani restaurant trade and became one of the most popular British curries, often cited as an entry point for those new to spiced food because of its gentle heat. The British version is typically milder and creamier than the original, using coconut milk and more sugar than traditional Mughal korma.

content.text: Cook the onion paste until it is very soft and golden before adding any other ingredients: this is the foundation of the sauce. The yoghurt should be added off the heat or over very low heat and stirred in gradually to prevent it from splitting. Use chicken thighs rather than breast: they stay tender through long braising.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless, cut into large pieces

content.text: Blend the onion, garlic, and ginger with a splash of water to a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pan over medium heat. Fry the onion paste for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until it turns golden and begins to stick to the pan.
Add the ground spices and cook for 1 minute. Add the chicken and stir to coat. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until sealed.
Stir in the ground almonds, then the coconut milk. Bring to a simmer. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir in the yoghurt. Season with salt. Scatter with coriander and serve with basmati rice and naan.
